findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed the coffee bar triple sink uses Bleach (Chlorine) but they do not have test strips to measure the concentration of Chlorine in the triple sink. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and acquired test strips during the inspection. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizing solution can be accurately determined with a test kit or other device
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following areas with an accumulation of soil residues:
(i) Back area staircase storage area has dust hanging from the walls.
(ii) 1ST REPEAT: Dairy walk-in cooler shelves have an accumulation of soil residues.
(iii) Dairy walk-in cooler floor underneath the shelves have an accumulation of soil residues.
(iv) Vents in several standing display coolers have an accumulation of dust.
(v) Bottom grates in several standing display coolers have an accumulation of soil residues.
PIC was notified, and stated that several of these areas are due for cleaning soon. PIC will have these areas cleaned by the next routine inspection. Ensure that Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Coffee: Observed an employee turned off the faucets with their bare hands after hand washing. The employee was educated that a barrier must be used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that the proper hand washing procedure is always used.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Coffee: Observed multiple wet wiping cloths stored on the counter. The employee working was educated and the wiping cloths were moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wiping cloths are always held in sanitizing solutions between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION.

Coffee: Observed powders for drinks stored with the scoop handles in direct contact with the powder. The employee was educated that all scoops for ready-to-eat foods must be stored to prevent contamination. The inspector suggests storing the scoops outside of the container. Ensure that scoops are stored with the handles above the top of the powder by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Back area: Observed the shelving in the back area walk-in cooler (connected to the dairy display coolers) have an accumulation of debris on the shelves for the dairy display cases. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Bakery: Observed the walk-in freezer floors have an accumulation of food residue underneath the shelving. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the floors are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Observed four cans of corn that had expired on 09/28/2024 on the shelves. These cans were removed from the shelf and moved to the back during the inspection. The inspector educated about the importance of checking expiration dates to ensure that foods are safe and honestly presented.

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Coffee: Observed scoops stored with the handles directly in powders. The powder goes into drinks without cooking or any other kill step for bacteria. The inspector discussed with the employee who moved the scoops into a position where the handles were not in contact with the powders. The scoops must to stored in this position at all times. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Cut room: Observed the ice machine has an accumulation of soil residue on the inside (upper left side). The ice machine must be cleaned to sight and touch. The inspector will return on 10/15/2024 to check that the ice machine has been cleaned. 


4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Retail: Observed rotisserie chickens stored in a heat lamp table below 135F. The rotisserie chickens had internal temperatures between 108F to 111F. Hot foods must be hot held at 135F or above. The chickens had been on the table since about 9am. The rotisserie chickens were voluntarily discarded during the inspection. 

For information about the equipment see violation #33.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Coffee: Observed milk and half & half opened more than 24 hours ago lacking proper date marks. The employee working stated the milk and half & half were opened several days ago. The inspector educated the employee and both containers were date marked during the inspection. Ensure that foods held at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Retail: Observed rotisserie chickens stored in a heat lamp table below 135F. The ambient air temperature of the table surface was about 137F which the PIC stated is significantly lower than the usual temperature. The PIC will be scheduling immediate service. Rotisserie chickens (or any other temperature control for safety foods) CANNOT be stored in the heat lamp table until it is serviced and hot holding foods at 135F or above. The inspector will return on 10/15/2024 to ensure the heat lamp table is functioning. 

For information about the food see violation #21.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Coffee: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available in the entire coffee area. The inspector educated the employee about the importance of sanitizer buckets for wiping surfaces. They also discussed the proper procedure for cleaning dishes (wash-rinse-sanitize). The manager filled up a sanitizer bucket for the coffee area from the bakery sanitizer dispenser during the inspection. The employee was instructed to fill up the bucket at the bakery everyday and check the bucket consistently using test strips. It should be dumped and remade on a regular basis. They were also instructed to transfer sanitizer from the bakery to the triple sink when washing dishes. The manager stated they have been working on getting a sanitizer dispenser installed in the coffee area. The inspector encourages that a dispenser be installed or sanitizer containers/tablets are available in the coffee area. 

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Bakery: Observed the drawer under the prep table holding clean utensils was soiled with food debris. The bakery employee cleaned the drawer during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
During the inspection, inspector observed that the hand sink in the coffee shop appeared to be soiled and dry. Inspector touched small pieces of paper at the bottom of the sink which were dry to touch. The operator stated that hand washing had occurred since the lunch rush. After questioning the employee, inspector was informed that hand washing was occurring in the neighboring triple sink instead of in the hand sink due to repairs being needed for the sink. Hand washing may only occur in designated hand washing sinks which are properly stocked. Ensure that hand washing sinks are clearly designated and that all staff understand that hand washing may ONLY occur in designated hand washing sinks. Inspector will return on 12/04/2023 to evaluate progress toward compliance. 

2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector observed there to be no hand soap in the soap dispenser at the hand sink in the coffee shop. Inspector discussed with employee who stated that the dispenser had been previously working that day but must have run out. Hand sinks must be stocked with hand soap at all times to facilitate proper hand washing. Ensure that hand sinks are stocked with both paper towels and soap during all operational hours. Inspector will return on 12/04/2023 to check hand sinks. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The ice machine upper baffle above the freezing tray is observed to have a significant accumulation of black mold. The majority of the interior of the ice bin was observed to be clean except this area. Ice machines/ice bins must be cleaned and sanitized often enough to prevent the accumulation of any mold from occurring. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces (include ice) are cleaned and sanitized at the proper frequency to prevent contamination. During the inspection, operator effectively cleaned and sanitized the entire ice machine. The violation has been corrected and no further follow-up is required at this time. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed temperature via infrared in the dairy cooler exceeding 41 degrees F. Temperatures ranged from 45 to 50 degrees F via probe. Items held out of temperature include but are not limited cheeses, yogurts, Jello and other dairy products. Inspector checked different areas of large yogurt containers to determine if foods have exceeded 41 degrees for an extended period of time. Operator contacted technician who arrived and stated that the cooler has been in defrost since approximately 1:00 pm. The cooler is scheduled to defrost at this time for x1 hour. However, the cooler malfunctioned and was "stuck in defrost" since 1:00 pm. Temperatures were checked by inspector at approximately 2:30. No food temperatures exceeded 50 degrees F and all temperatures following corrective action were trending downward. Technician ensured that the cooler is now functioning properly. Additionally, operator spoke with technician and informed inspector that the monitoring temperature on the coolers was set to notify them at 60 degrees F. This has been corrected so that facility will be notified if temperatures exceed the 41 degree threshold. Violation has been corrected on site. No additional follow-up required. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Under the triple sink in the coffee shop, a wet wiping cloth was observed sitting on the floor. The wiping cloth appeared crusty and molded. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer at proper concentration at all times.

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The countertops in the coffee shop are observed to have a layer of dust, debris and residue underneath equipment in hard-to-reach areas. These non-food contact surfaces are required to be cleaned often enough to prevent such accumulations from occurring. Ensure that all nonfood-contact surfaces of counters and other equipment are cleaned as often as necessary.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed areas of the floor and walls in the coffee shop under counters and equipment to have a significant accumulation of residue and debris. Further, inspector observed there to be a significant amount of cobwebs which have accumulated on the ceiling and plumbing. These areas of the physical facility must be cleaned often enough to prevent any such accumulation from occurring. Ensure that the facility remains clean especially in hard-to-reach areas that become neglected. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
In the upright cooler in the coffee shop, inspector observed a package of personal medication and a container of personal food stored amongst food intended for service. These items were immediately removed by person-in-charge after discussing the violation. Corrected on site. No further follow-up required at this time. Ensure that personal items are stored in designated areas within the cooler to prevents contamination of foods intended for public consumption. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Coffee Bar:
Inspector observed that the ice scoop was properly removed and stored in a metal container but the metal container had a small amount of water at the base of it which was light brown and cloudy in appearance. Operator was instructed to clean the container and the ice scoop and ensure that the container is clean any time a utensil is stored within it. The scoop was removed, cleaned and the container was cleaned during the inspection today. No further follow up is required; corrected on site. Ensure that ice scoops and other food contact items are stored in clean locations.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Coffee Bar:
Inspector observed a container of white granules sitting on the countertop in a glass container with a metal lid and a flip spout. Operator advised that the container holds sugar. As a white granulated substance that can easily be mistaken for another, this container must be labeled to indicate that it is sugar. Inspector observed a small semi-transparent container in the lower cabinet toward the service area of the coffee bar. The container contained a white powder with no indication of what the powder is. This container must be labeled. Ensure that all foods outside their original container are labeled if they are not easily recognized. 

This is a repeat violation from the previous inspection dated 08/03/2021

3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Bakery: 
Inspector observed that the vents in the bakery have an accumulation of debris, especially the vent next to the fire alarm. Vents are above food preparation areas. There is no active debris blowing from the vents onto food or other surfaces. Clean the vents and nearby tiles which have dust accumulating and ensure that cleaning occurs frequently enough to prevent dust from building up.

Coffee Bar:
The piping above the coffee bar is observed to have a buildup of dust. These are horizontal pipes running above the coffee prep and dish washing area. There is no dust actively falling onto food preparation or other surfaces. Ensure that these pipes are cleaned often enough to preclude the accumulation of dust. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
No signed employee reporting agreements on file. Keep verification that staff have been educated on illness reporting.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
COFFEE: Two tubs of unidentifiable powders observed near the hot water dispenser. Label to indicate contents.
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
COFFEE: Two wet wiping cloths observed on the counter. CORRECTED-- Discussed storage with PIC. Cloths moved to sanitizer solution or laundry receptacle.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. [C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
COFFEE: Container of single service knives and spoons observed with eating ends pointing up. CORRECTED-- Discussed with PIC. Utensils were rearranged to reflect proper storage with handles pointing out.
4-904.11: (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. [C]
